newsitem.title: CHINA: JILIN SEES NO RISE ON PRODUCT PRICES.
newsitem.headline: JILIN SEES NO RISE ON PRODUCT PRICES.

text.p: Jilin Chemical Industrial Co Ltd sees no rise in product prices in the second half after price falls in certain products hurt profits in the first six months of 1997, vice general manager Lu Qirong said on Friday.
The petrochemical giant posted a 69.5 percent fall on interim net profit to 103.35 million yuan.
"Production of the company will be suspended for routine annual maintenance for a month in the second half of the year," Lu said, declining to give an earning forecast for the year.
But starting next year, maintenance would take place every two years instead of annually, he said.

Prices for petroleum products fell an average of about 8.5 percent in the first six months to 1,535 yuan per tonne and Petrochemical and organic chemical product prices dropped 17.5 percent to 3,381 yuan per tonne in the same period, Lu said.
Products under the two categories accounted for over 70 percent of the company's sales output in the first six months.
An increase in the cost of crude oil to 1,005 yuan a tonne from 885 yuan, higher depreciation and financial expenses also dragged the interim net down, he added.
In the second half Jilin Chemical would strength its cost control and increase production of downstream products with higher profit margins, chairman Liu Shulin said in a statement.

"The management also intends to implement operational strategies by adopting more proactive hand effective measures to develop the existing product markets, expand sales volume and increase market share," he added.
